archetype.name: Gunslinger (play-extending)
archetype.definition: Mayfield holds the ball, extends plays with his feet and keeps firing into tight windows. That produces big seasons when his accuracy holds, and sacks and turnovers when it doesn't.

report.headline: A broken start built on sacks and misses, now paused by a thumb
report.take:
Mayfield's career has swung between peaks and slumps. In 2024 he posted 0.207 EPA per play, 8th in the league, with a 5th-best bad-throw rate. His 2022 season was the other end, at -0.125. The constants are an aggressive arm, real scrambling value (378 and 382 rushing yards the last two seasons) and a pressure-to-sack rate that has always sat in the bottom third. Through three games of 2026 he landed hard on the slump side. His -0.274 EPA per dropback ranks 40th of 43, and Tampa is 0-3 without a single cover.

Two things are driving it, and only one is new. The sacks are partly who he is: his pressure-to-sack rate has been 0.357 to 0.391 every year in Tampa. This season it is 44.8%, the worst of 36 charted passers, and his 2.99-second time to throw is his slowest since 2020. The accuracy is the new part. His bad-throw rate of 19.8% is last among qualifiers and well above anything in his career, and it climbed every week: 7.4%, then 21.2%, then 30.3%. The Minnesota game, against the defense now ranked 1st, was the low point. He was blitzed 26 times, sacked six times and posted a -14.8 CPOE.

The numbers hide a few things in both directions. Week 1 looked tidy at 23 of 28, but his intended air yards were just 4.7, and three lost fumbles did most of the damage. That fumble total is the kind of thing that rarely repeats at that rate. His only good passing came with the game out of hand: +0.288 EPA when trailing by 9 or more, against -0.471 within one score. Third down (-0.475) and the red zone (-0.548) were where drives died. He was also better under center (0.48 success rate) than in shotgun (0.31), which points to the protection and spacing out of shotgun as part of the problem.

Now he is out with a dislocated thumb. Jalon Daniels started Weeks 4 and 5, and the estimated return is October 25. His snap share dipped to 94% in Week 3, his last start. The dossier doesn't say when the thumb was hurt or whether it was bothering him that day. Either way, three games of tape against two top-half defenses and the league's best is a thin sample next to eight seasons of history. The open question is whether the accuracy spike was injury, opponent or decline. His career says the floor is closer to his 2025 level (0.089 EPA) than to this.

strengths.title: Track record well above this start
strengths.body: His last three Tampa seasons ran 0.13, 0.207 and 0.089 EPA per play, all far above -0.274. A three-game sample that included the league's top defense shouldn't outweigh that. Expect real upward regression when he's healthy, though probably to a 2025-type level rather than 2024's.

strengths.title: Scrambles still move the chains
strengths.body: Nine scrambles for 63 yards and four first downs, at +0.237 EPA each, have been one of the few positive plays in this offense. It matches back-to-back seasons of roughly 380 rushing yards. That is a stable trait, though a thumb injury shouldn't change his legs.

strengths.title: Better when under center
strengths.body: Under center he completed 78.3% of passes with a 12.3 CPOE and a 0.48 success rate, against 0.31 from shotgun. That's only 25 plays, but it lines up with an offense whose run game ranks 7th. A heavier diet of under-center work is the obvious lever for his return.

concerns.title: Pressure turns into sacks too often
concerns.body: An 11.9% sack rate (42nd of 43) and a pressure-to-sack rate worst among charted QBs are an exaggerated version of a career trait. He holds the ball looking for the big play, and here the extra time isn't buying completions downfield: 21.4% completions on deep balls. Some of this regresses, but he will always take more sacks than average.

concerns.title: Accuracy fell off a cliff
concerns.body: A 19.8% bad-throw rate is last in the league and far above his 11.1% in 2024 and 15.1% in 2025. It got worse each week, peaking at 30.3% against Minnesota's 26 blitzes. That is the stat to watch on his return, especially after a thumb injury.

concerns.title: Drives stall when it matters
concerns.body: His EPA was -0.475 on third down (30.3% conversions, facing 8.7 yards to go on average) and -0.548 in the red zone. His only efficient passing came when trailing by 9 or more. Long third downs are a byproduct of the sacks, so this improves only if the protection-and-hold-time issue does.

trend.note: His CPOE went 14.0, 4.2, then -14.8 across his three starts while his bad-throw rate climbed from 7.4% to 30.3%. He hasn't started since Week 3, with Daniels taking Weeks 4 and 5.

nextGame.headline: Sidelined for Pittsburgh; Daniels inherits a beatable but windy matchup
nextGame.body:
Mayfield is ruled out with a dislocated thumb, with an estimated return of October 25, so the Week 6 game against Pittsburgh isn't his. On paper it would have been a reasonable spot. The Steelers' defense ranks 18th in EPA and gives up the second-highest explosive pass rate in the league, though it is 7th against short passes and allows just 12.1 fantasy points a game to quarterbacks. The early forecast calls for 20 mph wind with 30 mph gusts, which would cut into any downfield game regardless of who starts. It is five days out, so treat it as a hint.

For Tampa, the relevant fact is that Jalon Daniels makes a third straight start. Pittsburgh is thin in the secondary, with CB Jamel Dean out and S DeShon Elliott on injured reserve, and DT Derrick Harmon is also on IR. That helps whoever is under center. Mayfield's own matchup questions wait until his return.

keyMatchups.title: Explosive-play leak in Pittsburgh's secondary
keyMatchups.body: Pittsburgh allows explosive passes at the second-worst rate in the league, and its secondary is missing Dean. That is the opening for Tampa's offense this week. When Mayfield returns, it is the kind of matchup his aggressive style needs.

keyMatchups.title: Wind could flatten the passing game
keyMatchups.body: Sustained 20 mph wind with 30 mph gusts, if it holds, pushes both teams toward the run. Tampa's run game ranks 7th in EPA, so that suits it. The forecast is early and could change.

nextGame.watch: Whether Mayfield returns to practice ahead of the October 25 target, and in what capacity. A thumb injury makes his grip and ball security the first thing to check when he's back.

restOfSeason.body:
Assuming he returns around Week 7, the realistic expectation is a quarterback closer to his 2025 self: mid-pack efficiency, around 6.8 yards an attempt and a steady 20-plus rushing yards a game. The 3-fumbles-in-one-game start and the league-worst bad-throw rate should both regress toward his norms. The sacks probably won't fully regress, because holding the ball has always been part of his game. A defense ranked 5th should keep games close, which removes the garbage-time padding but also the need to chase.

The risk is that the thumb either explains the accuracy collapse, which is good news once it heals, or lingers and keeps it there. Week 3's 30.3% bad-throw rate under heavy blitzing is the version of him to fear. His under-center work, his strong results on throws to the middle of the field and Godwin's 0.483 EPA per target are the parts worth building around.
swingFactors: How the thumb affects his accuracy and grip on return
Whether Tampa leans into under-center and the run game

confidence.note: Only three games, one against the top defense, then an injury that may have played a part. His return date is an estimate.
